tone-generator-probe.context: A pen shaped tone probe with a pointed tip and sound waves coming from it. Used by network and telephone installers to trace and identify cables in walls and patch panels.

wire-gauge.context: A round wire gauge disc with sizing slots cut around its edge and a centre hole. Used to check the thickness of wire and sheet metal in electrical and metal work.

punchdown-tool.context: A punch down tool pressing a wire into the slot of a terminal block. Used by network and telephone technicians to terminate cables on patch panels, keystone jacks and wiring blocks.

perfboard.context: A square prototyping board filled with a regular grid of holes. Used by makers and students to solder and build small circuits without making a custom printed circuit board.

breakout-board.context: A small breakout board with one chip in the middle and a row of pins along one edge. Used to make a tiny chip easy to wire on a breadboard or connect to a microcontroller.

development-board.context: A long narrow microcontroller board with pins down both sides and a USB port at one end. Used for prototyping, learning to code hardware and building maker projects.

fpga-chip.context: A programmable logic chip with a grid of logic cells inside and pins on every side. Used for field programmable gate arrays, custom digital hardware and hardware design topics.

system-on-chip.context: A chip divided into several functional blocks, with pins around the edge. Represents a system on a chip that combines processor, graphics, memory and radio in one package.

silicon-die.context: A bare silicon die with a central core and bond pads around its rim. Used for semiconductor manufacturing, chip design and wafer fabrication topics.

pcb-panel.context: A panel of four identical circuit boards joined by small break away tabs. Used for PCB manufacturing, panelisation and assembly line topics.

smd-reel.context: A reel of surface mount parts with the carrier tape trailing off. Used for component stock, pick and place machines and electronics manufacturing.

reflow-oven.context: A conveyor reflow oven with a circuit board riding in and heat rising above. Used for surface mount soldering in electronics manufacturing and PCB assembly.

solder-paste-stencil.context: A thin metal stencil with a row of pad cutouts and a squeegee blade resting on it. Used to print solder paste onto circuit boards before placing surface mount parts.

solder-paste-syringe.context: A solder paste syringe with a bent needle squeezing out a small dab. Used to dispense solder paste or flux for surface mount soldering and rework.

etching-tank.context: A tank of etching liquid with a circuit board hanging inside and bubbles rising. Used for making home made printed circuit boards by chemical etching.

pcb-holder.context: A board holder with two clamp arms gripping the edges of a circuit board. Used on the workbench to hold boards steady while soldering, testing or repairing.

project-enclosure.context: A plastic project box with screw holes in its corners and its lid lifted off. Used to house finished electronics projects and circuit boards.

pcb-standoff.context: A hexagonal threaded spacer with a screw stud at one end. Used to mount circuit boards above a case or stack boards with a gap between them.

pcb-antenna.context: A circuit board with a meandering zigzag copper antenna trace. Used for printed antennas on wireless modules, wifi and bluetooth boards.

rf-module.context: A radio module board with a metal shield can and a coiled spring antenna. Used for wireless links, remote controls and low power radio in maker and iot projects.

gps-module.context: A small GPS board with a square ceramic patch antenna and signal arcs. Used for satellite positioning in trackers, drones and maker projects.

infrared-receiver.context: A small infrared receiver with a domed lens on its face and three legs. Used to pick up signals from remote controls in televisions, appliances and electronics projects.

real-time-clock-module.context: A real time clock board with a coin cell battery holder and a clock chip. Used to keep the date and time in microcontroller projects when power is off.

motor-driver-board.context: A motor driver board with a tall finned heat sink and screw terminals. Used to run dc and stepper motors in robots, rc vehicles and cnc machines.

relay-board.context: A relay board with boxed relays and screw terminals along one edge. Used to switch lamps, pumps and mains loads from a microcontroller in home automation projects.

breadboard-power-module.context: A small power module with a barrel jack whose pins plug into the power rails of a breadboard. Used to feed 3.3 or 5 volt power to prototype circuits.

usb-to-serial-adapter.context: A small adapter board with a USB plug at one end and a row of pins at the other. Used to connect a computer to the serial port of a microcontroller for programming and debugging.

debug-probe.context: A debug probe box with a flat ribbon cable ending in a pin connector. Used to program and debug microcontrollers and embedded boards.

chip-programmer.context: A chip programmer box with a lever socket on top holding a chip. Used to write firmware to memory chips and microcontrollers before they go on a board.

el-wire.context: Glowing electroluminescent wire looping out of a small battery pack. Used for costume lighting, cosplay, signs and wearable glow effects.

humidity-sensor.context: A small humidity sensor box with a grid of vents on its face and three pins. Used to measure air humidity and temperature in weather stations and climate projects.

gas-sensor.context: A round gas sensor with a mesh dome cap on a small board. Used to detect smoke, alcohol, methane and other gases in alarms and air quality projects.

accelerometer.context: A sensor chip with three axis arrows pointing up, right and diagonally. Used for acceleration, tilt and motion sensing in phones, wearables and drones.

magnetometer.context: A sensor chip with a compass needle drawn on top. Used for digital compasses, heading sensing and magnetic field measurement in phones and drones.

hall-effect-sensor.context: A flat three legged hall sensor beside a bar magnet, with a field line between them. Used to sense magnets for position, speed and contactless switching.

flex-sensor.context: A long thin flex sensor strip bent in a gentle curve, with two pins at one end. Used to measure bending in data gloves, wearables and robotics.

force-sensor.context: A round force sensing pad on a thin tail ending in two pins. Used to detect presses, squeezes and weight in buttons, seats and robot grippers.

load-cell.context: A rectangular load cell bar with a hole through its middle and a cable out one end. Used to measure weight in digital scales and force testing.

pressure-sensor.context: A pressure transducer with a round sensor body on a threaded fitting and a cable out the top. Used to measure pressure in pipes, pumps and hydraulic systems.

rain-sensor.context: A rain sensor board with two interlocking comb traces and raindrops falling on it. Used to detect rain in weather stations, garden irrigation and window controls.

sound-sensor.context: A sound sensor board with a microphone capsule on it. Used to detect claps, noise level and audio in electronics projects.

color-sensor.context: A colour sensor board with a central sensor chip surrounded by four small lights. Used to detect the colour of objects in sorting machines, robots and projects.

image-sensor.context: An image sensor chip with a glass window showing a grid of pixels. Used in cameras, phones and machine vision to capture pictures.

water-level-sensor.context: A thin water level sensor board with parallel traces, dipped into wavy water. Used to measure liquid depth in tanks, pots and flood alarms.

flame-sensor.context: A flame sensor board with a dark round infrared receiver facing a small flame. Used to detect fire and open flames in alarms and robotics projects.

current-transformer.context: A split ring current clamp around a cable, with two output leads. Used to measure electric current without cutting wires in energy monitors and meters.

keypad-matrix.context: A flat membrane keypad with a grid of keys and a ribbon tail. Used for pin entry, door locks and number input on microcontroller projects.

spectrum-analyzer.context: An instrument screen showing sharp peaks above a baseline, with knobs beside it. Used to view signal frequencies in radio, audio and rf testing.

lcr-meter.context: A handheld LCR meter with a coil symbol on its display and two clip leads. Used to measure inductance, capacitance and resistance of components.

frequency-counter.context: A bench frequency counter with a row of digits and a round input connector. Used to measure the frequency of signals in radio and electronics labs.

insulation-tester.context: A handheld insulation tester with a large dial and a lightning bolt warning mark. Used by electricians to test cable insulation at high voltage.

test-leads.context: A pair of pointed test probes joined by their lead wires. Used with multimeters and other meters to take measurements on circuits.

oscilloscope-probe.context: A slim oscilloscope probe with a hook tip and a short ground clip lead. Used to connect an oscilloscope to test points on a circuit.

logic-probe.context: A pen shaped logic probe with two indicator lights and a clip lead. Used to check whether digital signals are high, low or pulsing.

test-lamp.context: A test lamp with a long pointed metal probe and a clear handle holding a small bulb. Used by mechanics and electricians to check for voltage in car and low voltage circuits.

electronic-load.context: A bench electronic load with a large fan vent, a display and a knob. Used to test power supplies and batteries by drawing a controlled current.

wattmeter.context: A round analog wattmeter with a needle and a W below the pivot. Used to measure electrical power in watts.

esd-wrist-strap.context: An anti static wrist band with a coiled ground cord ending in a clip. Worn when handling circuit boards and chips to prevent static discharge damage.

anti-static-bag.context: A resealable anti static bag with a warning triangle on it. Used to package and store circuit boards, chips and computer parts safely.

anti-static-mat.context: An anti static work mat with a snap stud in one corner and a cord to a ground symbol. Used on workbenches to safely drain static while repairing electronics.

smith-chart.context: A Smith chart: a circle filled with arcs and circles that meet at its right edge. Used in rf engineering to plot impedance and design matching networks.

bode-plot.context: A Bode plot: two stacked graphs, gain flat then falling above and phase dropping below. Used to show the frequency response of filters, amplifiers and control systems.

eye-diagram.context: An eye diagram: signal traces crossing to leave an open eye shape in the middle. Used to judge signal quality and jitter in high speed data links.

timing-diagram.context: A timing diagram: stacked square pulse traces lined up in time. Used to show digital signals, clocks and protocols in datasheets and logic analysers.

desoldering-pump.context: A desoldering pump: a long plunger tube with a pointed nozzle and a release button. Used to suck molten solder away when removing components.

desoldering-braid.context: A small spool of flat braided copper wick with a length hanging down. Used to soak up solder when cleaning pads and removing parts.

soldering-iron-stand.context: A spiral coil holder for a soldering iron on a base with a sponge tray. Used on the workbench to rest a hot iron safely and clean its tip.

tip-cleaner.context: A round tip cleaner cup filled with coiled brass wool. Used to wipe and clean a soldering iron tip without cooling it.

flux-pen.context: A flux pen with a felt tip and a drop of flux falling from it. Used to apply flux to pads and joints so solder flows cleanly.

hot-air-station.context: A hot air rework station: a box with a display and a handheld hot air wand. Used to remove and solder surface mount parts during electronics repair.

soldering-gun.context: A pistol shaped soldering gun with a trigger and a loop shaped tip. Used for heavy wire joints, stained glass and quick soldering jobs.

solder-joint.context: A solder joint: a component lead through a board pad with a smooth cone of solder around it. Used for soldering guides, quality inspection and through hole assembly.

solder-pot.context: A small solder pot on legs holding molten solder, with heat rising above. Used to tin wires and dip solder parts in a molten bath.

fume-extractor.context: A small fume extractor with a fan grille drawing in wisps of solder smoke. Used on workbenches to pull soldering fumes away from your face.

spudger.context: A spudger: a thin prying stick with a flat tip at one end and a point at the other. Used to open device cases and lift connectors during phone and laptop repair.
